root.note: From khadd ‘cheek’. It is not connected with the Almohads, the 12th-century dynasty, despite the similar sound.

history: An almohada is the place for your cheek. Arabic khadd meant ‘cheek’, and al-mikhadda, ‘the pillow’, is built on it. Andalusian Arabic passed it to Spanish, with the article al- stuck to the front, as in so many words from al-Andalus. The Arabic kh sound, like Spanish j, became a written h inside the word, and that h is silent today: you say almoada. Because the word sounds a little like the Almohads, the Muslim dynasty that reached Spain in the 12th century, people sometimes connect the two, but the cheek is the better explanation. Portuguese and Galician almofada kept a consonant there.
historyEinfach: Almohada means ‘pillow’. It is an Arabic word. Khadd means ‘cheek’ in Arabic. A pillow is where you put your cheek. With the Arabic word for ‘the’, al-, Spanish made it one word: almohada. The h in the middle is silent, so we say almoada. Portuguese says almofada.

elsewhere.text: The article al- is inside the Spanish word, as in alcalde.
Portuguese almofada kept an f where Spanish has a silent h.
